A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMAAT study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support comparison, including matching relocated pseudocode and renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RMAAT benchmark results, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses and neuron–astrocyte simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Text-task ablations and an evaluated RLT + AMRB variant in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: Segmented memory-token processing, astromorphic attention, retention scaling and AMRB remain unchanged. The retention-factor equation clarifies the existing procedure, and Algorithm 1 moves from Appendix D into Section 3.4 without changed steps. RLT + AMRB is introduced as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five LRA tasks and neuroscience simulation scenarios. The added ablations use the already-covered Text (4K) and Retrieval (8K) tasks; they do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Section 4.2 adds RLT + AMRB, which combines the RLT baseline with the retention factor and AMRB, and reports comparisons against RLT and RMAAT.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled configurations that remove retention or replace AMRB with BPTT on Text, plus a Retrieval control combining standard linearized attention with retention and AMRB. Existing benchmark metrics, segment settings and Appendix E hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 extends the retention-factor and BPTT ablations from Retrieval to Text and adds RLT + AMRB to examine the contribution of astromorphic components. The earlier sequence-length tests and Appendix F sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals or formal significance tests. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include Text accuracy declining from 65.9% to 64.9% without retention, Text peak memory of 22.0 GB with BPTT versus 5.1 GB with AMRB, and RLT + AMRB Retrieval accuracy of 79.2% at approximately 3.4 GB with RMAAT-like throughput. Existing main and appendix table values and simulation findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the ambiguous capacity/area-under-the-curve description with Equation (6), explicitly normalizing each LTP increment by the sum of increments over T segments and defining increments at cycle boundaries. This is a limited refinement of the mathematical definition; the remaining equations, complexity analysis and gradient discussion are retained.

C1.justification: The conclusion withdraws the claim of 'state-of-the-art average accuracy,' instead claiming 'strong average accuracy' and restricting validation to the evaluated benchmark setting. The central RMAAT, retention-factor and AMRB contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 identifies true streaming or online processing with unknown total sequence length as requiring future extensions, making a concrete applicability boundary explicit. Section 3.3 also more clearly distinguishes the abstract saturation model from its implementation as a transformer compression schedule.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-availability link and explicitly documents the retention factor's normalization and cycle-boundary calculation. Appendix E retains the same hardware, software versions, optimizer and hyperparameter values.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references on neuromodulated RNNs and synaptic plasticity, including Miconi et al. (2020) and Duan et al. (2023). It distinguishes RMAAT's simulation-fixed modulation structure and timescales from those approaches and clarifies its relationship to earlier astrocyte-attention and associative-memory work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the introduction, contribution descriptions, memory-mechanism explanation and conclusion. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, acknowledgments are added, and author/header text is revised. Most prose and the overall section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing diagrams are resized or repositioned, Figure 2 receives a substantially expanded caption, and Algorithm 1 is relocated and reformatted. Appendix figures and tables receive continuous numbering, with layout and text-size adjustments. No experimental plots or result tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The added Text and RLT + AMRB ablations modestly strengthen evidence about component contributions. The explicit retention definition and code-access information improve reproducibility documentation, while the narrower performance claim and streaming qualification improve claim calibration. These are useful, bounded gains; the central method, benchmark coverage and principal results remain unchanged.
